label: D1 step before an upcoming a2 choice
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), on roughly half of D1 steps: those where the agent is about to choose a2. Dev: P 0.84, R 0.94, F1 0.88, mass recall 0.95. The upcoming action is the agent's own computed choice, which is allowed. The only-observed alternative (phase == D1) & (prev_action == 2) is weaker (F1 0.82, mass recall 0.79). The D1 policy logit choice < -1.5, i.e. already leaning toward a2, gets F1 0.85. Misses are weak activations at D1 steps where a1 is chosen right after a2 trials, mostly on switch trials. False positives are a2 D1 steps with no activation, many early in the episode: rate is low in trials 0-9 and the feature is almost silent in the first 3 trials. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.95), and the feature is silent when value > 8.1. It does not fire on a1-bound D1 steps (rate 0.02) or at GO/D2.

issues: Upcoming choice versus previous choice. When the action switches, the feature follows the PREVIOUS choice (observed), not the upcoming one. D1 steps where the agent switches to a2 after an a1 trial ((phase==D1)&(action==2)&(stay==0), 12106 steps): precision is only 0.156. D1 steps where it switches to a1 after an a2 trial ((phase==D1)&(action==1)&(prev_action==2)): precision 0.62. The test-split misses output shows both patterns over and over. So the label 'before an upcoming a2 choice' gets the two disagreeing cases backwards.

The claim that the observed-only predicate is 'weaker' is an artifact of the windowing. prev_action is -1 on the window's first trial (rel -3, about 20% of D1 steps), so (phase==D1)&(prev_action==2) cannot fire there. On rel > -3, where the previous choice is known, the observed predicate wins: prev_action==2 gives F1 0.817 (P 0.868) against action==2 at F1 0.786 (P 0.830).

A hybrid that uses prev_action, falling back to the upcoming action only where prev_action is unknown in the window, beats the original. (phase==D1)&((prev_action==2)|((prev_action==-1)&(action==2))) scores dev F1 0.910 / mass recall 0.976, and test F1 0.906 / mass recall 0.971, against the original's 0.874 on test.

The firing rate also drops late in the episode, which the explanation does not mention. The rate in trials 90-99 is 0.115, against about 0.18 in the middle of the episode. Precision of the original predicate is 0.59 for ep_trial>=90 and 0.29 for ep_trial>=95. The early-episode silence is real (ep_trial<10: precision 0.41), but the explanation describes only the early side.

Verified as stated: the feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 rates are 0.000). The D1 rate before an a1 choice is low, though about 4% of a1-bound D1 steps fire and they are mostly a1 switches after a2 trials. Magnitude is flat (median 0.95). The value > 8.1 claim is trivially true (only 9 steps). Also checked: firing is lower when S1 is good during long a2 runs (D1, action==2, prev_action==2: good==1 precision 0.82 against good==2 precision 0.91), but this is a small effect.
